# RFC 2578 section 3.7 ends a comment at a second pair of hyphens or at
# the end of the line. A comment that runs to the end of the file leaves
# no declaration boundary after it that can be trusted, which is why it
# costs the file.
#
# This fixture is contrived, and the contrivance is the finding. A
# comment can only run to the end of a file under the paired rule, and a
# file is only ever read under the paired rule when that reading loses
# less than the end-of-line one. Losing less means resolving more
# conditions of severity error or worse, and the only such conditions the
# lexer raises are the two unterminated ones — either of which stops the
# framer before it can raise a second. So the end-of-line reading has to
# reach severity-error conditions from the framer instead, and then still
# be fatal.
#
# That is what the body does: read under the end-of-line rule, the
# comment's continuation lines are live text — a declaration beginning
# with a number, which nothing can classify, and a brace nest past the
# depth bound, which costs the file. Read under the paired rule, all of
# it is one comment, and what is left is the last comment, which nothing
# closes.
code smi/paired-comment-mode
code smi/unterminated-comment
